title: feat(openai): add Sign in with ChatGPT through Responses

commit.messageHeadline: feat(auth): route renewable OAuth grants by provider policy
feat(openai): add Sign in with ChatGPT preview
feat(codex): bridge host-owned token sharing to Responses
feat(status): show the selected model endpoint
feat(openai): register and reuse SIWC OAuth clients
docs(openai): explain authentication choices and identity
refactor(siwc): clarify sign-in choices and credential preparation
fix(openai): reconcile SIWC with main and remove unused auth export
test(openai): await expired SIWC wizard before retry
merge: reconcile SIWC maintenance test with main
feat(ui): show provider accounts and connection methods together
test(ui): select API key from provider connection dialog

Reviewed `4f9fb43c4afb890106a48029e0c5798eba97a227`. Three findings remain:

1. **P1 — Production type checks fail in the new OpenAI code.** The new refresh hook can return `null` although its contract requires a credential ([source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4f9fb43c4afb890106a48029e0c5798eba97a227/extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts#L1170-L1176)). The stream wrapper adds `replayResponsesItemIds` to a `SimpleStreamOptions` literal that does not declare it ([source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4f9fb43c4afb890106a48029e0c5798eba97a227/extensions/openai/responses-stream.runtime.ts#L29)), and the JWKS cast does not establish the required `keys` field ([source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4f9fb43c4afb890106a48029e0c5798eba97a227/extensions/openai/token-sharing-oauth.runtime.ts#L106)). [Production-type CI](https://github.com/stevenlee-oai/openclaw/actions/runs/35908249141/job/107343297097) reports all three diagnostics. Preserve the non-null refresh contract and narrow/type the other two inputs at their owning boundaries.
2. **P2 — The sign-in note can outlive the OAuth timeout and retain port 8080.** [The note await](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4f9fb43c4afb890106a48029e0c5798eba97a227/extensions/openai/token-sharing-oauth.runtime.ts#L374-L390) is not raced with `owner.signal`. Gateway wizard notes await client acknowledgement. If that acknowledgement never arrives, the five-minute timeout cannot reach the listener cleanup; personal connect expires only after 15 minutes. Other sign-ins can consequently fail to bind the port during that interval. Apply `withOAuthLoginAbort` to this wait and test an unacknowledged real wizard note through timeout and port reuse.
3. **P2 — Catalog refresh preserves stale grant classification.** [The new `authFlow` projection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4f9fb43c4afb890106a48029e0c5798eba97a227/src/agents/models-config.providers.secrets.ts#L271-L277) reads the captured credential, while successful catalog preparation overlays only the refreshed bearer. If refresh reduces a sharing grant to identity-only, the OpenAI catalog still sees token sharing and advertises Responses models instead of returning the empty/auth-rejected result. Carry refreshed grant metadata alongside the bearer and cover the downgrade through the prepared catalog resolver. Runtime inference independently rejects identity-only credentials; this is not a claimed authorization bypass.

**Simplicity Audit:** The existing credential, refresh, prepared-route, wizard, and relay owners are reused. No separate credential store or unnecessary parallel subsystem was established; the snapshot and timeout ownership gaps above need repair.

**Test Audit:** All 40 changed test files were reviewed for value and assessed **keep**; no merge/delete recommendation. This does not mean they pass. CI also reports changed-test type/fixture/assertion failures and lint failures. Missing proof includes timeout listener release, catalog downgrade after refresh, and composed persisted-grant-to-physical-egress rejection.

Validation: source/diff review, direct inspection of pinned Codex 0.154.0 source, whitespace check, and CI log diagnosis. CI logs cited above ran synthetic merge `882f1e6f09853ee186b5e22a07916d62673466b3` containing this head, not a direct head checkout. No local fork code or live SIWC inference was executed. The PR's user-reported live Mac sign-in is acknowledged; live inference, refresh, and allowance attribution remain unverified. No fixes applied.

Codex: addressed the three findings in `001f129c7059edb8867a848dec40095cdcb6f147` and refreshed the branch against current main.

1. **Production types:** the native refresh hook has a required, non-null credential contract; SIWC uses a typed provider-specific replay option; fetched JWKS data is narrowed before passing it to `jose`. Core, UI, and plugin production type checks pass. The replay override remains explicit because the normal provider policy can otherwise enable server item references.
2. **Unacknowledged sign-in note:** the note now races the existing OAuth deadline. A real setup-dispatch/WizardSession integration regression fails before the fix and passes afterward, proving the listener can bind again without acknowledging the old note. Its real socket uses an isolated port, reused across both attempts, so parallel OAuth tests cannot collide.
3. **Catalog refresh:** preparation carries the refreshed credential's `authFlow` with its bearer for the selected profile, including clearing stale flow. Both sharing-to-identity-only and removed-flow regressions fail before the repair; the full catalog-context suite passes 4 tests.

The review also repaired wrong-account adoption/reconciliation and reconnect ownership during refresh, and kept SIWC credentials out of Codex quota probes. Independent correctness and maintainability reviews found no remaining actionable findings in these fixes.

Validation limits remain explicit in the PR body: full changed-file validation is blocked by file-length growth checks; a native concurrency fixture times out with both candidate and main relay implementations; live inference, refresh, allowance attribution, and composed persisted-grant-to-physical-egress proof are not claimed. The user-confirmed Mac sign-in is separate evidence. No merge performed.
